results.title: Trace-context headers never break requests (spec API-OBS-04)
results.desc: Valid and malformed traceparent both handled without error
results.prose: Random spec draw: api-server-observability.spec.md (API-OBS-04 - inbound traceparent/tracesstate must join the trace when valid and be ignored, not adopted, when malformed; either way the request proceeds). I sent both shapes to the api-server: a well-formed W3C traceparent and deliberate garbage. Both were processed cleanly - same controlled 401 as any unauthenticated request, no 5xx, no rejection caused by header handling. The span joining itself is not visible from outside, but the user-side contract (malformed tracing headers never break requests) holds, and it composes with the TRACEPARENT env-forwarding we verified in battery N2.
results.steps: curl api-server with valid traceparent + tracestate; curl with malformed traceparent; both must return normal status codes (no 5xx).

results.title: Route-gated Running state (upstream #1023)
results.desc: Gateway healthy with working route - the new Running precondition
results.detail: Health grpc=0, healthy=True; route serving all battery RPCs
results.prose: Upstream #1023 tightens the spec: a gateway's Running state now requires the GRPCRoute to be Accepted and route_address populated - the health loop previously checked only the shared Gateway API object. This gateway predates that change but satisfies its spirit verifiably: Health reports healthy and the route serves every authenticated RPC this cycle. When fleet gateways pick up the tightened check, Route-not-yet-Accepted gateways will correctly stay non-Running instead of passing readiness on a route that cannot serve.
results.steps: rpc Health; confirm healthy status; note all battery RPCs traverse the route successfully.
